seo.title: EXTANT — Myanmar Djent & Metalcore | Official Site
seo.description: EXTANT — djent and metalcore from Myanmar, founded in Yangon 2015. Back from exile with a six-song concept album and the HAIYAR cry. Latest single P TRIPPER. Videos, lineup, history and REBEL DOG · BITE BACK merch.

copy.top-12: Yangon, Myanmar  //  Est. 2015  //  Djent & Metalcore
copy.top-13:
They left the scene, the crowd, and the place they called home.
Being away didn't end the music — it changed it.
copy.return-19: /haɪ jɑːr/ — a traditional Burmese boxing cry, shouted before the fight.
copy.return-21:
There was a time the band had to leave — the scene, the audience, and the place they called
          home. For a while the distance between EXTANT and the people who listened to them grew wider
          than any of them expected.
copy.return-22: It didn't end the music. It changed it. The band returns with a new sound, a six-song concept album, and a cry that runs the length of the record: HAIYAR. Shouted before the fight, not after it.
copy.return-23: This is the return. And it is only the beginning.
copy.return-26:
A concept record rather than a singles run — the first time the band has written to a single
          arc from end to end.
copy.return-29:
The band's own framing for the turn: a new direction, and a raw, unfiltered sound they have
          never made before. The Rubicon is the river you only cross once.
copy.return-32: Written, tracked, mixed and mastered inside the band — PZ on the desk, the same room that produced P Tripper.
copy.return-35:
Teasers, studio clips and singles go out through the band's own page and channel. No label
          pipeline in between.
copy.return-38: No release date announced yet — singles are landing first. P Tripper is out now.
copy.drop-44:
The first single of the return, and the loudest thing EXTANT has put on tape.
          Tracked, mixed and mastered in-house by PZ, shot and cut by No Worries with camera by
          FAT CAT. Five thousand plays inside the first day.
copy.drop-55: Available on Spotify, YouTube & all major streaming platforms.
copy.records-58:
Albums and singles under the EXTANT name, plus Novem Htoo's solo output. Where a
        record is still rolling out, only what the band has confirmed is listed here.
copy.records-62:
Six songs, one arc, and a new sound built in exile. Framed by the band as crossing the
            Rubicon — a turn they can't walk back.
copy.records-67: The record behind Back Off, mixed and mastered by TheBigBoyToy with lyrics translated by U Day. Video presented by Mi Joya Pictures.
copy.records-72: Novem Htoo’s solo single, released on 31 August 2023. The project connects his solo work with the musicians around EXTANT, including Japan of Idiots.
copy.records-77: Untie The Knot, Vengeance, This Is The War and Disregard — four Burmese-language releases in three months, mixed by Ko Ye Zaw Myo (Big Bag). Still the band's most-played material.
copy.vault-81:
Every official upload on the EXTANT channel, with titles, dates, running times and
        credits taken from the videos themselves. Previews are hosted here — hover a card on desktop,
        or bring it to the middle of the screen on mobile. Click for the full video with sound.
copy.vault-83: Nothing in this cut of the vault.
copy.unit-86: Novem Htoo, PZ, Min Khant and Oo Japan — the four players credited on the band’s recent music videos. Oo Japan is also known for his work with Idiots.
copy.unit-87: Regular crew No Worries · FAT CAT · Ko Kaung · Latt Pan Ni Production · Myo Wai Yan · Mi Joya Pictures · TheBigBoyToy · Ko Ye Zaw Myo (Big Bag)
copy.history-90:
Founded in Yangon in 2015. What follows is drawn from the band's public channel,
        page and press.
copy.history-93:
A five-piece built out of Myanmar's underground metal circuit, playing djent and metalcore in
            a scene dominated by pop and rock.
copy.history-95: Novem Htoo wins The Voice Myanmar
copy.history-96: Novem Htoo wins The Voice Myanmar Season 2 after a blind audition with Slipknot’s Spit It Out. In the final, he performs a song by Idiots — another connection between the two bands.
copy.history-99: Four releases in three months — Untie The Knot, Vengeance, This Is The War and Disregard — mixed by Ko Ye Zaw Myo (Big Bag). This Is The War becomes the band's most-played upload.
copy.history-102:
A live set from the TGIF show in Taunggyi lands in January. The coup follows in February.
            The band later described having to leave the scene, the audience and the place they called
            home — and the distance that opened up between them and the people who listened.
copy.history-105:
Novem Htoo releases a solo single on Burmese Guerrillas in collaboration with Artists' Shelter,
            featuring The BigBoyToy and Japan (Idiots) — out across Apple Music, Spotify, Tidal, Deezer and
            YouTube Music.
copy.history-108: Dog Eat Dog and Main Character Syndrome arrive five days apart in November — the first proper music videos with the current four-piece lineup, shot with Ko Kaung on photography and Latt Pan Ni Production on lights.
copy.history-111: Back Off lands in May off the Aggressive Evolution record. P Tripper follows on 29 August and clears five thousand plays in a day. Days later the band announces the return: a six-song concept album carrying the HAIYAR cry.
copy.merch-114: The streetwear arm around the band — graphic tees and carry built for the everyday, with the politics left in. Run out of Tak, on the Thai border. “If you dare to stand up for what is right, you are welcome here.”
copy.merch-118: Bold graphic print designed to deliver an unapologetic street aesthetic.
copy.merch-121: A graphic tee representing Daw Aung San Suu Kyi and her unbroken spirit.
copy.merch-124: Let your tee do the talking when you want your voice heard.
copy.merch-127: Built with maximum street vibe for your everyday carry.
copy.merch-129:
REBEL DOG runs an ongoing editorial series on where street culture
      actually came from, published to the page alongside the drops.
copy.merch-132:
The original oversized silhouette, and the first time baggy clothing was treated as a
          political act.
copy.merch-135: The legendary store where Fujiwara, NIGO and Jun Takahashi changed youth culture for good.
copy.merch-138:
How Hiroshi Fujiwara and NIGO rewrote global streetwear — limited drops, collaborations,
          exclusivity.
copy.merch-141: Myanmar's own line of protest, and why the brand still reads “still biting back”.
copy.merch-144: 12K followers · Run out of Tak, Thailand, on the Myanmar border · Orders go through the REBEL DOG page — mmrebeldog.com is registered but not serving yet.
copy.contact-147:
Festivals, gigs, features, press. Reach the band through the official
      page, or the merch line for anything REBEL DOG.
copy.contact-159: Solo catalogue · Revolution Means, Body Bags
copy.global-169:
Fan-built official-style site. Music, artwork and photography remain the property of EXTANT,
      REBEL DOG and their respective owners. Previews and full videos are both served from this site, at the highest
      resolution each was uploaded in. “Watch on YouTube” opens the band's own channel. Figures reflect public channel data at time of build.

members.name: Novem Htoo
members.bio: EXTANT’s vocalist and the winner of The Voice Myanmar in 2019. His blind audition brought Slipknot’s “Spit It Out” to national television. Before EXTANT, he sang with Myanmar metal band Nightmare; his work also includes solo releases and collaborations across the local rock scene.

members.name: PZ
members.bio: Low end and the desk. Mixes and masters the band's recent output, including P Tripper, Dog Eat Dog and Main Character Syndrome.

members.name: Min Khant
members.bio: Riffs, drop tunings and the djent-leaning rhythm work that anchors the newer material.

members.name: Oo Japan
members.bio: Oo Japan, known as Japan of the Myanmar rock band Idiots, plays drums with EXTANT. Credited as “Japan Idiots” on P Tripper, Dog Eat Dog and Main Character Syndrome, he connects the band’s rhythm section with Myanmar’s wider rock scene.
